questions.q: What is the primary reason positional encodings are necessary for Transformer models?
options: To increase the computational speed of the attention mechanism
Because self-attention is permutation-invariant and the model is blind to token order or spatial position
To reduce the memory footprint of the model during training
To convert integer coordinates into floating-point numbers for better precision
questions.answer: Because self-attention is permutation-invariant and the model is blind to token order or spatial position
questions.why: The lesson states that self-attention is a permutation-invariant operation where the model is 'blind to order' and does not know which token is first or last, making positional encodings necessary to inject spatial or temporal information.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the dimension of the 2D positional encoding vector $E_{2d}$ when constructed using the formula $[\sin(x \cdot f), \cos(x \cdot f), \sin(y \cdot f), \cos(y \cdot f)]$?
questions.why: The 'Under the hood' section explicitly states that the 2D encoding vector $E_{2d}$ results in a vector of dimension 4, consisting of two components for x and two for y.

questions.q: In the provided lab results, what is the specific vector value for the 3D positional encoding at the coordinate $(x=0, y=0, z=0)$?
questions.why: The 'Lab' section shows the result `enc_3d_first = [0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0]` and explains that since all coordinates are 0, all sine terms are 0 and all cosine terms are 1.

questions.q: Why are sinusoidal functions (sine and cosine) chosen for positional encodings according to the 'intuition' section?
options: They are the only functions that can handle negative coordinates
They are periodic and allow the encoding of a shifted position to be computed as a linear transformation of the original position
They produce unbounded values which help with numerical stability
They are computationally cheaper than linear functions
questions.answer: They are periodic and allow the encoding of a shifted position to be computed as a linear transformation of the original position
questions.why: The lesson explains that sine and cosine are used because they are periodic and, more importantly, the encoding of position $pos + k$ can be computed as a linear transformation of the encoding of position $pos$, which allows the attention mechanism to easily compute relative distances.

questions.q: Which ComfyUI module contains the class `VideoRopePosition3DEmb` that implements 3D Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) for video sequences?
questions.why: The 'In ComfyUI' section lists item 3, stating that `comfy/ldm/cosmos/position_embedding.py` contains the class `VideoRopePosition3DEmb` which implements 3D RoPE for video sequences.
